FileAnalysis.description: How much of a file kv-cli could check.

oneOf.description:
YAML, `.env*`, TOML, INI/cfg, JSON and notebooks: scanned for
credentials only, so the scope is always zero.
A syntax error: audited on a partial parse. Also listed in `skipped`.
The file could not be read at all. Also listed in `skipped`.

FileResult.description: One resolved file and what the run concluded about it.

errors.description: This file's findings whose intrinsic severity is error.

scope.description: The run's scope counts for this file alone. They sum to `run.scope`.

status.description: The worst of this file's findings; `skipped` or `clean` when it has none.

warnings.description: This file's findings whose intrinsic severity is warning.

FileStatus.description:
What a run concluded about one file. Intrinsic, like a finding's severity:
`--strict` never changes it, because applying strictness is the reader's
decision.

oneOf.description:
No findings, and fully read. Not a compliance claim on its own: read it
with `analysis` and `scope`, since a file can be clean because nothing
in it was enforced.

key.description: The assignment target, when the finding came from a name rule.

oneOf.description: An environment-specific identifier written into the source.
A function whose name does not match a naming rule.

fingerprint.description:
Stable identity across runs. Excludes the line number on purpose - see
[`finding_fingerprint`].

framework.description: Framework profile that contributed the rule, when one did.

path.description:
Repository-relative, forward-slashed. Normalized before hashing so the
same file yields the same identity however the scan was invoked.

report_only.description: KV001 only. True when the function is governed but report-only (counted in functions_report_only); false when it is enforced. Absent on other codes.

severity.description:
Intrinsic severity, as emitted. `--strict` is a gating policy applied
by the consumer, not folded into this value or into the counts.

subject.description:
What about it: the required parameter for KV001, the detector name for
KV002 and KV003, the naming rule's name for KV004.

symbol.description:
The thing the finding is about, as data: the function name for KV001
and KV004, the assignment target or key for KV002 and KV003. Empty
when a value-pattern rule matched free-floating text with no binding.

IdentitySource.description: Provenance of each run-identity field: `"flag"`, `"env:NAME"`, or absent.

contract_path.description: `null` means the run used built-in defaults.

errors.description:
Findings whose *intrinsic* severity is error, regardless of `strict`.
Counts only `findings` - a skipped file's severity is on the entry
itself in `skipped`, not folded in here.

files.description:
Every resolved file, sorted by path, so `files.len() == files_scanned`:
the files that passed are listed, not only the ones that failed. Absent
from payloads before 0.9.0, so not required.

frameworks_detected.description: Framework profiles detected, and in how many files.

identity_source.description:
Where each identity field came from, so an absent value is
distinguishable from a wrongly-guessed one.

repo.description: `owner/name`, when known. The CLI cannot invent it.

schema_version.description: Payload shape. Bumped only on a breaking change.

skipped.description:
Files resolved for scanning that produced no findings because they
were not fully analysed. See [`SkippedFile`].

strict.description:
Whether the run was told to treat warnings as gating. Severities below
are reported as emitted; applying this is the server's decision.

tool_version.description: The binary that produced this run.

warnings.description: Findings whose *intrinsic* severity is warning, regardless of `strict`.

Scope.description:
Tally of scope decisions across a run.

Without this a green result is a claim with no evidence: a repository where
every governed function is framework-owned looks identical to one that
fully complies.

functions_exempt_framework.description: Excluded because a framework owns the signature.

functions_report_only.description: In scope, but a framework forbids auto-fixing them.

SkipReason.description:
Why a file contributed nothing to `findings`.

Two different concerns, kept distinct rather than folded into one
human-readable string: a syntax error is a claim about the *code* - the
file exists and was read, but only a partial parse was possible, which may
itself hide findings. An unreadable file is a claim about the *tool run* -
kv-cli could not open it at all, which is not a matter of degree.

SkippedFile.description:
A file that was resolved for scanning but produced no findings because it
was not fully analysed. Every resolved file appears either represented in
`findings` (implicitly, via `files_scanned`) or explicitly here - a file
can never simply vanish from the payload.

detail.description:
Human-readable elaboration - not to be parsed. `reason` is what a
server should key on.

severity.description:
Whether this counts toward the gate, on the same terms as a finding:
intrinsic, not altered by `--strict`. A syntax error is a warning by
default - it does not fail CI on day one, matching how KV003 was
introduced - and is promoted to gating under `--strict`. An unreadable
file is always an error: there is no lenient reading of "the tool
could not check this file".
